card: This pull request removes the temporary -persistmempoolv1 configuration option, which previously allowed nodes to dump mempool.dat in the legacy non-XORed format on shutdown. It cleans up deprecated code now that Bitcoin Core v26 and earlier versions requiring v1 files have reached end-of-life. Node operators can still upgrade from older releases because reading v1 files remains intact. The change only affects users attempting to downgrade to unsupported releases older than v27.
evidence: PR description: "-persistmempoolv1 was added in #28207 as a temporary option to allow downgrading to v26 and earlier, which can't read the XOR'ed mempool.dat. v26 has now been EOL for a while... docs have always stated that this was a 'temporary option that will be removed in the future'."
PR description: "Reading v1 files is still supported, so upgrading directly from an old version keeps the persisted mempool."
problem: The temporary `-persistmempoolv1` compatibility flag was introduced in PR #28207 solely to allow downgrades to Bitcoin Core v26 and earlier. Since v26 is end-of-life and unsupported, the option is obsolete technical debt.

risk.why: Users attempting to downgrade to EOL releases (v26 and earlier) will no longer be able to export mempools readable by those old versions.

scope_notes: Small mechanical cleanup removing a configuration flag, its documentation, and updating compatibility tests.
summary: Removes the `-persistmempoolv1` command-line option, stopping support for writing legacy non-XORed `mempool.dat` files on shutdown. Loading existing v1 mempool files remains supported for nodes upgrading from older releases. The functional test `mempool_compatibility.py` is also updated to test against v28.2.
